text: Fixture Bank Limited — Framework Alignment — DCAM
One assessment, four vocabularies. These are not four independent measurements — they are one evidence base expressed in four published
frameworks. The four overall figures landing close together is the correct result: the same answers, projected through the same eleven capability
pillars. What differs between them is emphasis and structure, which is what makes each one legible to a different audience.
Retained share is how much of the framework’s own definition of a dimension is in scope under this engagement’s layer. Scored share is how
much of what is in scope was actually measured. They answer different questions and are never combined: a dimension can be fully retained
and barely scored, or the reverse, and a single "coverage" number would hide whichever is worse.
All figures are on the DGIW 1-5 maturity scale. They are NOT rescaled to each framework’s own scale — DCAM scores 1-6 and COBIT 2019
uses capability levels 0-5. A DCAM component shown here as 3.2 is 3.2 out of 5, not out of 6.
What is published and what is ours
Framework names, codes and dimension structures are published content. The relative WEIGHTS applied to those dimensions
are Godaitec editorial judgement — none of these four frameworks publishes weightings for its own dimensions. The weights are
the first thing to challenge in review, and changing them changes every figure derived from them.
DCAM (v2.2) — Published structure recorded at MEDIUM confidence — verify before relying on it in an audit context.
FLAGGED FOR REVIEW. The eight components below are DCAM v2.2 as I recall it, and the exact published wording of several component
names is uncertain — 'Data Management Program & Funding' and 'Data Control Environment' in particular may differ in the source. DCAM
v3.0 reorganised the model and this is NOT v3.0; versionLabel says v2.2 deliberately rather than claiming currency. DCAM's capability and
sub-capability levels beneath each component are NOT authored here: I do not recall them reliably enough to put in front of an auditor, and
an absent level is recoverable where a fabricated one is not. The 1-6 scale is DCAM's six-point scoring (Not Initiated / Conceptual /
Developmental / Defined / Achieved / Enhanced) and I am reasonably confident in it.
Fixture Bank Limited — Framework Alignment — DCAM
Retained and scored share are separate columns on purpose. Retained is how much of the framework’s own definition this engagement’s scope
covers; scored is how much of that was measured.
A projected target appears only where EVERY capability pillar the dimension maps to under this layer carries a target set on the diagnostic; the
gap only where the dimension is also scored. A dimension with any unset pillar target shows neither — a target projected from part of its
mapping would be arithmetic over measurements that do not exist. The projected target is the same convex combination the score uses, applied

Why each dimension maps to the capabilities it does
Every row below was authored deliberately. A mapping a consultant cannot defend in a room is not a mapping, and this section is the room.
DCAM1 · Data Management Strategy & Business Case
Strategy and business case is P02's whole subject; nothing in this component falls elsewhere.
Funding model and programme mandate are strategy questions in P02.
Programme structure, resourcing and who is accountable for delivery is operating-model territory,
Business and data architecture — the model of the business and its data — is P03.
DCAM places the business glossary and the definition of critical data in this component; DGIW
Identifying the entities the business runs on is master-data work, P06.
Technology architecture is the platform and tooling estate, P10.
The architectural standards governing that estate remain P03.
DCAM expects the technology architecture to make data flow traceable, which is P07.
Fixture Bank Limited — Framework Alignment — DCAM
Data quality management maps directly onto P05.
The same BCBS 239 argument as DM11: evidencing quality to a regulator means evidencing it to
source. Banking-only, so DCAM5 retains 0.85 under core.
DCAM's Data Governance component is roles, authority and the governance forum — P01.
It also carries the mandate and its alignment to business objectives, which is P02.
The control environment is largely access, classification and protective controls — P08.
A control with no named owner is not a control; the accountability half sits in P01.
Demonstrating control effectiveness to a regulator requires traceable flow from source to report.
Banking-only, so DCAM7 retains 0.75 under core — the largest retained-share gap in this crosswalk
and the one most worth showing a client.
Analytics management and P11 AI & Consumption address the same capability.
Fixture Bank Limited — Framework Alignment — DCAM
What this assessment does not cover
Every leaf dimension of DCAM is both in scope under this layer and measured. Nothing in the framework is unaddressed.
DCAM is modelled at v2.2. Its capability and sub-capability levels beneath each component are deliberately NOT authored: they were not
recalled reliably enough to put in front of an auditor, and an absent level is recoverable where an invented one is not. DCAM v3.0
reorganised the model and is not what is represented here.
COBIT 2019 APO14 sub-practice titles have been checked against a public COBIT 2019 reference and corrected where they differed. They
have NOT been checked against the ISACA publication itself, which is the only source an audit function should accept — treat them as
verified secondhand, not as quoted. The five EDM governance objectives are high confidence.
The three DGI groupings used as parents are how the published DGI diagram arranges the ten components; treating that arrangement as a
formal level is a modelling choice, not published hierarchy.
